question_or_symptom: Why can a pinned Triton LLVM source still produce a different HSACO identity when it is exported below a repository that has a parent Git checkout?
observation: LLVM VCS revision discovery walks upward from an exported source directory and can find the amdgpu-sim root Git repository. With LLVM_APPEND_VC_REV enabled, the embedded LLD version string added the parent repository path and commit to the HSACO .comment section. The first fresh schema-8 attempt therefore generated a 5,648-byte hash-different image and the daemon rejected COMMIT even though removing .comment made the ELF bytes identical. Rebuilding the embedded LLD and Triton wheel with LLVM_APPEND_VC_REV=OFF restored the locked 5,384-byte image and passed two managed launches.
conclusion: A pinned source commit does not by itself isolate compiler provenance from the containing checkout. The generated code-object identity is also affected by linker VCS metadata and must be checked at the CMake cache, generated-header, and final HSACO layers.
decision: Configure Triton LLVM with LLVM_APPEND_VC_REV=OFF, require LLVM_FORCE_VC_REVISION and LLVM_FORCE_VC_REPOSITORY to remain empty, require the generated LLVM/LLD VCS headers to contain only undefines without a parent path or commit, and keep the exact HSACO SHA as a fail-closed admission gate.
invalidated_assumptions: A clean pinned child source export is sufficient to make compiler output independent of the parent Git checkout.
An HSACO hash mismatch necessarily indicates a code or descriptor change rather than non-loadable linker provenance metadata.
Reusing a partially built prefix after changing compiler provenance settings is equivalent to a fresh accepted install.
